solution:
Using $\cos^2\theta=1-\sin^2\theta$:
$$2(1-\sin^2\theta)+\sin\theta-1=0\quad\Rightarrow\quad -2\sin^2\theta+\sin\theta+1=0,$$
i.e. $2\sin^2\theta-\sin\theta-1=0$. Factorising,
$$(2\sin\theta+1)(\sin\theta-1)=0.$$
So $\sin\theta=-\tfrac12$ or $\sin\theta=1$. In $[0,2\pi]$:
- $\sin\theta=1$ gives $\theta=\tfrac{\pi}{2}$;
- $\sin\theta=-\tfrac12$ gives $\theta=\tfrac{7\pi}{6},\,\tfrac{11\pi}{6}$.

Thus $\theta\in\left\{\tfrac{\pi}{2},\,\tfrac{7\pi}{6},\,\tfrac{11\pi}{6}\right\}$.
hints: You get a quadratic in sin theta; factorise it.
